scene.room: kitchen in a 1938 California bungalow, remodeled, now opening to an adjacent open space on the right
scene.view: straight-on elevation of the sink wall, eye level, slight wide angle

camera.angle: perpendicular to sink wall, one-point perspective

lighting.primary: soft natural daylight through the window over the sink, late morning, Northern California
lighting.secondary: warm under-cabinet LED strip below upper cabinets, 2700K

elements.name: lower_cabinets
elements.type: shaker-style base cabinets, full run, drawers over doors
elements.color: Sherwin-Williams Dried Thyme SW 6186 (muted gray-sage green)
elements.hardware: aged unlacquered brass bar pulls on drawers, brass knobs on doors, darker burnished tone, not shiny gold
elements.detail: recessed toe kick in a darker sage

elements.name: upper_cabinets
elements.type: shaker-style upper cabinets running left of the window, extending to the ceiling with simple crown
elements.color: Sherwin-Williams Alabaster SW 7008 (warm creamy white), matching walls exactly

elements.name: left_tall_cabinets
elements.type: floor-to-ceiling shaker-style tall cabinets on the far left, replacing the former left wall, housing a fully integrated panel-ready Thermador refrigerator column with matching cabinet fronts
elements.color: Sherwin-Williams Dried Thyme SW 6186 (muted gray-sage green), matching the lower cabinets exactly
elements.hardware: aged unlacquered brass bar pulls, burnished tone
elements.detail: Thermador refrigerator concealed behind green cabinet panels; small discreet Thermador badge; no exposed stainless steel

elements.name: floating_shelves
elements.type: two thick floating white oak shelves, stacked, in the zone to the right of the sink only
elements.material: rift-sawn white oak, natural unstained, clear matte finish
elements.styling: stacked cream ceramic bowls, small potted plant with sage-green foliage, glass jar, one sage-green ceramic bowl, small brass object

elements.name: right_open_space
elements.type: the sink wall terminates just past the floating shelves; beyond that the wall is removed and the room opens into a bright adjacent living/dining space
elements.detail: open doorway-width transition, no wall on the far right, soft bright out-of-focus open room visible beyond, floor continues through as the same white oak

elements.name: backsplash
elements.type: handmade Moroccan zellige tile, 4x4 inch squares, tight grid, minimal grout
elements.color: warm white / weathered white with natural tonal variation from cream to ivory, glossy reflective glaze, slightly irregular handmade surfaces catching the light
elements.extent: standard height under upper cabinets; full height from counter to ceiling behind the floating shelves

elements.name: countertop
elements.appearance: polished off-white base with sparse, soft grey pencil-thin veining, subtle and understated, NOT bold marble veining
elements.detail: single seamless run, no visible seams

elements.name: sink_and_faucet
elements.type: white fireclay UNDERMOUNT sink under the window, mounted below the quartz countertop with a continuous quartz surface and no apron front
elements.faucet: aged unlacquered brass gooseneck bridge-style faucet, burnished patina

elements.name: window
elements.type: double-hung window centered over the sink, painted Alabaster trim
elements.view_through: soft green garden foliage, out of focus

elements.name: walls_and_trim
elements.type: smooth painted walls and simple 1938-appropriate trim
elements.color: Sherwin-Williams Alabaster SW 7008, eggshell walls, satin trim

elements.name: floor
elements.type: site-finished white oak plank flooring, 5 inch planks
elements.finish: natural unstained, clear waterborne matte finish, no orange or amber tones, matches the floating shelves

style_references: editorial interior photography, Architectural Digest quality
negative: no exposed stainless steel appliances in frame (Thermador fridge is panel-ready and concealed)
no farmhouse apron-front sink; the sink is undermount
no bold dramatic marble veining on the quartz
no upper cabinets on the right side of the sink (floating shelves only there)
no wall on the far right where the shelves terminate (it opens to another room)
no clutter, no people, no text or watermarks

output.notes: hold the exact paint relationships: sage lowers AND the tall left cabinets must read clearly darker and greener than the warm white uppers and walls; shelves and floor must be the same natural oak tone; the left is a floor-to-ceiling green cabinet run with a concealed Thermador fridge; the right side opens into an adjacent bright room with no terminating wall
